h1: Banging pipes or water hammer near a cylinder
title: Banging pipes or water hammer near a cylinder | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand banging pipes or water hammer near a cylinder. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Banging associated with outlet or valve closure needs a water-supply and pipework investigation, not an invented cylinder fault-code reset.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: Fast changes in water movement, incoming pressure and pipe support can influence the symptom. The cylinder may be nearby without being the failed component. A discharge or expansion concern should still be assessed on its own evidence.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Record when the bang occurs, which outlet is being used and whether recent work changed the pattern. Avoid adding a pump or adjusting pressure controls without a designed assessment.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Is pipe banging proof that the Megaflo cylinder vessel is faulty?
faqs.answer: No. Water movement, valves, pressure and pipe support can contribute; identify the origin before blaming or replacing the vessel.
